subtitle: Implement the host loop that turns structured model requests into bounded, observable local actions
description: Build and test a provider-neutral tool-call loop with a closed registry, schema validation, replay protection, visible failures, and stop budgets.

hashnode.seo_title: Build a Minimal, Testable Tool-Using AI Agent
hashnode.seo_description: Implement a host-controlled tool loop with validation, replay protection, failure traces, and explicit execution budgets.

visuals.caption: The model proposes the next move; the host controls whether and how it executes.
visuals.alt: A bounded tool-call sequence from task and model proposal through host validation, local execution, result tracing, repetition, or an explicit stop.

social.linkedin: A model does not hold your function pointer. It proposes an action; your application validates, authorizes, executes, records, and stops. Part 3 builds that boundary as a provider-neutral Python loop with six deterministic tests.
x_thread: A model does not execute your local tool. It proposes structured data; your host application decides what happens.
The minimal loop is: propose, validate, execute, observe, then repeat or stop.
Part 3 implements the boundary with a closed registry, JSON Schema validation, replay protection, failure data, and explicit budgets—without a live model or API key.

publication_submission_note: A framework-neutral, runnable lesson on the host-side authority boundary in tool-using agents, with current official sources, six deterministic tests, an accessible sequence diagram, and an extension exercise.
